response.content: The blind shark is one of the most elusive species of shark in New South Wales.
This shark gets its name from the milky colour of its eyes and the fact that they close their eyes when removed from the water.
This shark is mainly nocturnal and spends most of the daylight hours in crevices or under seagrass.
So seeing them out in the open like this is rare and has only ever been recorded very few times.
So this makes this footage unique.
These sharks primarily feed on mollusks and snails.
